summary: An action passage from a fiction novel, narrated in first person, in which the narrator disarms and kills guards inside the Grigoryan estate using a borrowed M16. After the narrator jams one goon's weapon and drops another, Grigoryan is left in a standoff and the narrator leaves the room. The narrator then switches the rifle to semiauto and picks off guards at range while clearing a path out of the estate. The narrator presents themselves as highly skilled and unbothered by killing.
one_line: First-person fiction action scene in which the narrator fights Grigoryan's guards with an M16 and clears a way out of the Grigoryan estate.
key_facts: The narrator wrenches an M16 away from a goon, and the momentum carries the rifle toward Goons #1 and #2 stock first.
The narrator's M16 had been set on full auto, and Goon #1 is killed when the narrator fires a burst into him.
Goon #1 falls back through a glass bookcase after being hit.
The narrator jams Goon #2's weapon by hitting it with the M16, so Goon #2's trigger pull produces nothing.
Grigoryan, the brother of the narrator's antagonists, says 'Impressive' with a voice shaking a little, and is left in a standoff.
The narrator says 'Bye now' to Grigoryan and slides out of the room while keeping an eye on him.
Grigoryan has a cigarette dangling from a corner of his mouth as the narrator leaves.
The narrator switches the M16's selector lever to semiauto, reasoning that automatic fire is for chewing up furniture rather than being deadly.
The narrator claims an M16 can hit a target six hundred meters away when the shooter is a good shot.
The narrator describes themselves as 'a fucking computer program' when it comes to guns.
The narrator states that three goons were neutralized in about two and a half seconds.
The narrator needs to get off the Grigoryan estate grounds, assuming Grigoryan raised every alarm before entering the room.
The narrator compares the sequence of shots to 'a particularly artistic mathematical proof'.
